scope.description: Five-voter cluster whose leading node is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a snapshot predating the membership change, isolated with one committed voter immediately after the restart. After both sides acknowledge a client write, the partition heals and the event reports, per side, whether the log store still holds that side's acknowledged entry, whether the FSM applied it, and the derived applied-without-log operand. Run with the flag on and off.
assumptions: A successful Apply is an acknowledgement to the client.
A truncated log suffix with a retained FSM application is the divergence signature being looked for.
Two seconds of healed time is a fair minimum for the two sides to exchange AppendEntries.
excluded: Any claim that the entries are never lost; only this schedule and window are observed.
Entry contents at the conflict index, which the probe reports as empty.

basis.prefix: The harness reuses the multi-voter scenario construction and the two-sided apply, then scans each side's log store between FirstIndex and LastIndex for the entry that side acknowledged and searches that side's applied slice for the same bytes, emitting minority_log_has_entry, minority_fsm_has_entry, applied_without_log, majority_log_has_entry, majority_fsm_has_entry and majority_applied_without_log together with the leadership, acknowledgement and divergence flags. No production logic is modified.
basis.responsibility: The library owns the durability of an acknowledged entry: if a replica applies an entry that its log no longer holds, the replicas' states diverge and the acknowledgement was not durable.

comparisons.description: The majority-side leader must not end up having applied an entry its own log no longer holds; the defect prediction is that it has.
The isolated node must not end up having applied an entry its own log no longer holds; the defect prediction is that it has.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side never acknowledges an entry, so its log cannot hold one.

before.description: Five-voter cluster whose leading node is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a snapshot predating the membership change, isolated with one committed voter immediately after the restart. Once the isolated node is leader and the majority side has its own leader, a client Apply is issued on both; the partition is healed, and the event reports whether both sides acknowledged. Run with the flag on and off.
assumptions: The isolated node's rebuilt configuration is the three-voter snapshot configuration, so two votes commit there while the committed configuration needs three.
A successful Apply is an acknowledgement to the client.
Waiting for both sides to hold leadership is a legal partition shape, not an injected fault.
excluded: FSM divergence and lost-entry claims; the applied-slice comparison at the conflict index did not line up and is not used.
Entry contents at the conflict index, which the probe reports as empty.

prefix.before: The harness reuses the multi-voter scenario construction (MakeClusterCustom with Peers 3, CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs; one deliberate Snapshot; MakeClusterNoBootstrap(2) merged with FullyConnect and two AddVoter calls; Shutdown and NewRaft on the same stores with a fresh inmem transport; Partition isolating the restarted node plus one committed voter with that pair reconnected). It waits for the isolated node to be leader, waits up to three seconds for a majority-side leader, applies a distinct command on each side, heals by reconnecting all transports, waits two seconds, and emits mvdiv_after_heal with both leaders' presence, both apply outcomes, the derived both_sides_acknowledged operand, the conflict index, the applied slice lengths and the FSM divergence flag; no production logic is modified.
prefix.after: The harness reuses the multi-voter scenario construction and the two-sided apply, then scans each side's log store between FirstIndex and LastIndex for the entry that side acknowledged and searches that side's applied slice for the same bytes, emitting minority_log_has_entry, minority_fsm_has_entry, applied_without_log, majority_log_has_entry, majority_fsm_has_entry and majority_applied_without_log together with the leadership, acknowledgement and divergence flags. No production logic is modified.

responsibility.before: The library owns the acknowledgement it gives a client and the guarantee that a committed entry survives; with a stale rebuilt configuration both depend on a quorum of an obsolete membership.
responsibility.after: The library owns the durability of an acknowledged entry: if a replica applies an entry that its log no longer holds, the replicas' states diverge and the acknowledgement was not durable.

before.description: Two partitioned sides must not both acknowledge client writes while one of them holds only a minority of the committed configuration; the defect prediction is that both do.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side has no leader, so only the majority side acknowledges.

after.description: The majority-side leader must not end up having applied an entry its own log no longer holds; the defect prediction is that it has.
The isolated node must not end up having applied an entry its own log no longer holds; the defect prediction is that it has.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side never acknowledges an entry, so its log cannot hold one.

revision_reason: The probe now measures survival of each side's acknowledged entry: the event reports whether the isolated node's own log still contains its entry and whether the majority-side leader's log still contains its own, each alongside whether that node's FSM applied it, giving an applied-without-log operand on both sides. Scenario, isolation, waits and the two-sided apply are unchanged.
